text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A cyclist was run over and killed by a jeep of the security police. The incident is being investigated.
- The U.S.-Baltic charter may be completed by autumn, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Ronald Asmus said during his visit to Tallinn.
- An Estonian-Finnish joint study reveals that stress, living conditions and hard work are considered the most important factors contributing to illnesses.
- The privatisation agency selected the management of the state-owned metal export firm Emex to privatise 51 percent of the firm's shares. A competing German bid was rejected.
- The rates for central heating for individuals will be increased from August. The rates for corporate users will be correspondingly reduced.
- The eighth children's song and dance festival ended in Tallinn on Sunday. There were approximately 30,000 participants.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann addressed the UNO General Assembly in New York on Tuesday and presented Estonia's achievements in environmental protection and sustainable development.
- Two car dealerships, Fakto and Asmer, will merge.
